translations.word:
Insurance Corporations and Pension Funds|Insurance corporations include all units engaged in all forms of life insurance and non-life insurance, such as fire, marine, accident, health, liability, and casualty insurance; fidelity and surety insurance; insurance agents and brokers; institutions serving insurance intermediaries; and advisors to policyholders.
Pension funds refer to funds that are established independently or separately from the units created by the organization. These funds have their own assets, liabilities, and transactions. Pension funds are established to provide retirement benefits to specific groups of employees. They may be managed or organized by the employer, or jointly managed by the employer and the employees, with regular contributions from both. These funds do not include retirement arrangements for employees of private or public units that do not have a separate and organized pension fund, nor arrangements where the reserves are added to the employer’s reserves or invested in securities issued by the employer. As an exception to this rule, separate pension funds for government employees are included even if most of their assets are invested in securities issued by the government.
